81261.subject: Who is Winning Tokenized Equities?
81261.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

**Who is winning in the tokenized equities boom?** 

Looking at weekly tokenized equity spot volume by chain, three different chains have at times held the pole position. Solana from the start of the year through June, BNB was in charge for July and August, and Robinhood chain took the lead in September. Since, both BNB and Solana rotated the top spot, with Base growing share and now shortly behind these top 3. 

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/4b655cbd-a21a-4b1b-a13e-3789f4f9b495/image.png?t=1792672968)
Caption: 

The same is true when looking at tokenized equity spot volume by DEX. Raydium and Meteora rotated leadership on Solana from the start of the year into June, Native took charge during BNB’s boom in July, and Uniswap became the leader with memestock season on Robinhood chain during August and September. With the recent rise on Base, Aerodrome now ranks 2nd behind Uniswap, while former leaders Raydium and Meteora, who once accounted for a combined share of 80% of this market, now only account for 10%. 

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/5a4d5c6c-dea6-4212-b97d-361a1fbc63e1/image.png?t=1792672968)
Caption: 

Going even further, no single issuer is winning this market, either. Since the start of the year, leadership in tokenized equity volume by issuer has rotated across xStocks, PreStocks, Backpack, bStocks, and Robinhood. 

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d5c03ced-a0ee-4253-8c5a-2cf4f72f31e0/image.png?t=1792672968)
Caption: 

So which chain, DEX, or issuer is winning? Monthly tokenized equities volumes have grown for nine consecutive months, and September cleared $25B, roughly 100x the level at the start of the year. Leadership keeps rotating across chains, DEXs, and issuers, but the pie keeps expanding. Losing the top spot by market share hasn’t meant losing ground in absolute terms. For example, Solana’s volume in September still exceeds the level during its months in pole position. While Raydium and Meteora’s combined share fell from 80% to 10%, combined volumes for these two venues just cleared 100% more volume than in their prior record month in June. In a market growing this fast, a rising tide lifts all boats, and everyone can win.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/1dbff7d8-5ed6-4c74-850c-9f1119bf50fc/image.png?t=1792672968)
Caption:

Crypto Biz: Crypto projects are shutting down, but Bitcoin treasury
 companies keep raising millions
81254.body:
Crypto Biz Newsletter

Автор: Cointelegraph


Автор: Cointelegraph

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/crypto-biz-projects-shutting-down-bitcoin-treasury-companies-4jm7c?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3B3eVhBsRtRM6e49Ne20L%2BXQ%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=0TuEavKkCzVIs1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mvjkkhbo~of-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mvjkkhbo-of
  
Crypto companies are facing very harsh financial realities in 2026. At least 82 projects have shuttered this year, with many running out of funding or failing to generate enough revenue to survive.  That contrasts with the situation with some Bitcoin treasury companies, which continue to attract capital. Strive has raised $630 million through a preferred stock offering, while Japan’s Metaplanet is expanding into the US market through a deal that would give it control of Nasdaq-listed Super League. Both companies are pursuing strategies built around accumulating Bitcoin, even as other parts of the crypto industry struggle to stay in business. However, capital-raising ability isn’t consistent across the Bitcoin treasury sector. Bitcoin’s roughly 53% decline from its October 2025 peak pushed several companies’ market net asset value (mNAV) ratios below 1, making it harder to raise capital through new share offerings. At least 82 crypto projects have shut down in 2026 Crypto researcher Stacy Muur has identified 82 digital asset projects that have shut down so far in 2026, spanning decentralized finance, blockchain infrastructure and Web3 gaming. The list includes Balancer, Radiant Capital, Neon EVM and Step Finance. Blast, which once held more than $2 billion in assets, also closed shop after concluding it had no credible path to financial viability. Separate research from DeFiLlama identified 100 project closures this year, including 40 over a 90-day period. The projects had collectively raised about $1 billion in funding yet generated just $250 million in lifetime fees. The most common reasons cited for shutting down included a lack of product-market fit, low revenue and depleted funding. The closures come amid a prolonged crypto bear market, with Bitcoin falling from a record above $126,000 a year ago to below $60,000 as recently as June. Although market conditions have improved in recent months, many projects still face funding shortages and struggle to sustain operations. Hey Friend! This is edition 100 of Adrian’s DeFi Alpha. Thank you for reading along, some of you since the very first one. A hundred weeks of me telling you to be patient, and Bitcoin still likes to test that advice every single week. This week it passed the test. Bitcoin is up about 41% from its June low of $58k, while the Nasdaq barely moved over the same stretch. Last week it swept down to $79.8k, and the buyers at $80k were buying it faster than lightspeed. The ETF buyers are back too. After roughly $936 million of outflows between October 7 and October 16, the spot ETFs took in about $1.07 billion in just three sessions this week. Though not everything is green. Stablecoin balances on exchanges are at their lowest of the year, and the altcoin froth from September has turned into fear. In the Market Overview I look at a source of support for stocks that most crypto investors ignore: Companies buying back their own shares. And in the Alpha section I explain the investment case for GRASS, with an update on Collector Crypt before that. Let’s get into the broader picture and how to set up for the coming week: ️ ⚡ On today's Episode: 📈 Macro Update – US companies authorized a record $1.305 trillion of buybacks this year, and midterm-year fourth quarters averaged 6.6% for the S&P 500 since 1950. Bitcoin is up 41% since June 30 while the Nasdaq is up 1%. 🔊 Crypto Pulse – Spot ETFs took in about $1.07 billion in three sessions after $936 million of outflows.
